accept: aortic stenosis with angina and syncope

findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy with strain pattern in lateral leads

echoTasks.find: Heavily calcified aortic cusps with restricted systolic opening on two dimensional imaging
Dense late peaking high velocity jet on continuous wave Doppler from the apical window
Concentric wall thickening with preserved cavity size and calcified valve in short axis

auscultation.added: Fourth sound from the stiff ventricle
auscultation.murmur: Harsh ejection systolic murmur grade 4 of 6 at the right upper sternal edge radiating to the carotids

exam.general: Elderly man, slow rising pulse, no distress at rest, arcus senilis noted
exam.other: Carotid shudder palpable, blood pressure equal in both arms, lungs clear
exam.precordium: Sustained apex beat displaced laterally, systolic thrill at the base
exam.pulse: Slow rising 68, small volume, anacrotic, no radio femoral delay

history.a: Chest tightness on walking uphill for one year, two faints in the field in three months, breathless on exertion
history.q: Describe the chest symptoms and any fainting

history.a: No palpitation, no orthopnoea, sleeps on one pillow
No known hypertension or diabetes, no prior heart checks
Beedi smoker for 30 years, stopped last year, no alcohol
Wife has arthritis, sons work as drivers, no early cardiac deaths in the family
Still works half days in the field, worried about losing income if advised rest
history.q: Work and what matters most to you

keyPoints: Explain that angina with syncope in severe stenosis marks high risk and needs urgent cardiology referral
Advise against strenuous exertion and dehydration while awaiting valve replacement
Treat coexistent hypertension gently, avoiding vasodilators that drop preload before review
Refer for surgical or transcatheter valve replacement assessment per the ESC valvular guideline
Counsel the family about the procedure, recovery time, and the need for lifelong follow up
management.model: Urgent cardiology referral for valve replacement with exertion restriction and gentle comorbidity control meanwhile

sources: ESC guideline on valvular heart disease, in own words
ASE guideline on valvular stenosis, in own words
stem: A 68 year old farmer from rural Punjab presents with exertional chest tightness and two recent faints while working. A harsh ejection systolic murmur radiates to the carotids, the pulse is slow rising, and the second sound is soft.
teaching: Angina plus syncope plus exertional dyspnoea is the classic severe aortic stenosis triad
A slow rising pulse with a harsh basal murmur radiating to the carotids is the bedside signature
Peak velocity above 4 m per s defines severe disease and matches the model output used for grading
Symptomatic severe stenosis needs valve replacement, not watchful waiting
title: Severe aortic stenosis with angina and syncope
